questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose Canada to explore the nature and wildlife there, since that is my main interest in Biology.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was on exchange to McMaster University, which was a nice university. It was located in the city Hamilton, which is a city that I was very disappointed when discovered. It is filled with homeless people, drug dealers and addicts and I didn't feel safe there, which had a huge negative effect on my semester abroad.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Tour of campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was lucky, because overall for many it was very difficult to find something.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That the city of Hamilton is very sketchy, and getting home late can feel unsafe, when you're not on campus. I recommend, if living off campus, live in the area Westdale, it's safer, but the housing is very competitive there.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *

Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Had to fill out some information, and that was fairly easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A contact person to e-mail.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Got the courses I wanted, so very successful

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is pretty easy, so I don't have any special advice for it, just to follow the instructions and deadlines.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had a level 1, 2, 3 and 4 course. Level 1 was extremely easy, level 2 was easy compared to danish level, level 3 was easy as well. My level 4 course, which to me was the most interesting one, was way more difficult, and the only course I had, where I really had to put in a lot of effort to follow along in the course.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Mostly lectures, and the tutorials are mainly about presentations, so not a lot of work in tutorials, either you had to present or listen to a presentation. I had labs in my level 1 course, which was more sitting and working either by yourself or with other people in the course, which was more like danish labs.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1G03 - Earth and the Environment
2GG3 - Natural Disasters
3DD3 - Communities and Ecosystems
4X03 - Environmental Physiology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Environmental Physiology was really interesting to me and a course where I learned a lot of new things, which I can use in my future career.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The outdoor club offered a lot of nice hikes and canoe trips, which I really enjoyed.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Free fitness on campus. A lot of social activities, such as bbqs to participate in to meet other students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Algonquin canoe trip.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Get out of Hamilton to reload. I took a trip to the west - Vancouver, Whistler, Kelowna, Banff and Jasper, which I can definitely recommend. A 10 day trip in the reading week. Also took a weekend trip to Montreal which is also a very nice city to explore.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to the people in your courses, they are hard to meet outside of there.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Small-talk. As a dane I don't do a lot of small-talk, but Canadians love that and can continue forever, I had to get used to that.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Canadians are very nice people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
I would tell them about how sketchy Hamilton is and advice them to live on campus or in Westdale.
Be sure to save money for travels to explore other sides of Canada.
Participate in social events.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Friendships.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Hamilton's sketchyness.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Generally I would not recommend going here. University is good, but for me Hamilton is just a city I won't remember for anything particularly good, sadly. Go somewhere else in Canada, that country has so much to offer - and that is not located in Hamilton.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
